newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries in London lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries in London lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Treasuries were slightly lower on profit-taking in London on Wednesday as the market continued to digest the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates steady.

"The market at first saw a little bit of profit-taking from the New York close. We are down just a small amount, but there is reasonablly high volume and good two-way trade," said one London-based trader.
By 0930 GMT December T-bond futures were quoted 5/32 down at 108-15 in automated trade, while December Eurodollars were down two basis points at 94.16, compared with the Chicago close.
The spread of 10-year U.S. yields over Germany was around 73 basis points by the same time.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. long bond was quoted at 93-30 to yield 6.994, compared with 96-25 in Tokyo and 97-01 in New York.
"Some customers are asking 'Has the Fed lost credibility here? Are they not fighting inflation?'" said the trader, referring to the Fed's decision on Tuesday to keep interest rates unchanged.

The trader said he personally believed such fears were unfounded and that Fed chairman Alan Greenspan was acting consistently with his publicly expressed view that the economy would slow in fourth quarter.
"In the end nothing has changed (as a result of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday)," the trader said.
"Forthcoming economic numbers will be of the utmost importance with the next non-farm payrolls data (for September) (on October 4) being a very big focus for the market," he said.
Nick Benton, a trader with BankAmerica, said Treasuries were marking time pending the U.S. opening after some selling from the Far East.
He said the market was slightly off in the sector from one to five years.
He said he expected further possible yield curve steepening, probably within the next two or three weeks.
"We expect the two-year Treasury note auction (at 1745 GMT) to go relatively well," Benton added.
The Treasury was scheduled to auction $18.25 billion of two-year notes, followed by $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Thursday.
